scope: All numbered sections and all checkbox proposals in the three SRS documents, all 25 explicit Comprehensive contracts, all eight AutoArchitect pillars. Repeated heading copies preserve additional_lines. No omitted placeholder is invented.

VALIDATE.reviewed_requirement: Keep typed validated input, explicit units, isotope masses, charge/multiplicity/electron parity, provenance and atom maps. QCSchema and QCIO are separate versioned models; XYZ may enter through a validated converter with required metadata. Fingerprints are candidate filters, never a proof of graph isomorphism.
VALIDATE.cons: Requires adapters and explicit missing-data states.
VALIDATE.risks: Incorrect atom mapping or unrecorded topology inference can corrupt every derived property.

ML.reviewed_requirement: ML engine/model changes require versioned model cards, element/charge/spin domains, independent validation, force/energy checks and out-of-domain handling. Keep ML optional; use reference calculations for publication claims.
ML.cons: Training, calibration and model maintenance are substantial.
ML.risks: Low ensemble disagreement can coexist with large systematic error; model transfer can remove real minima.

UQ.reviewed_requirement: Report calibrated prediction intervals only from matched held-out residuals or a documented uncertainty model with covariance. Otherwise report uncertainty unknown. ML variance, diagnostic thresholds, method-to-method differences and MAE are not confidence intervals.
UQ.risks: Fabricated or miscalibrated precision would mislead assignments and publication claims.

BUDGET.reviewed_requirement: Use an immutable versioned budget with authenticated actor, explicit limits and allowed recovery plans. SHA-256 checks integrity; authentication/signing is separate. Reserve costs atomically before dispatch; allow previously approved batch policies.
BUDGET.risks: Hash-only authorization is forgeable; GUI-only approval prevents unattended runs.

RESOURCE.reviewed_requirement: Estimate actual per-engine memory/scratch/VRAM with cgroup and scheduler limits, empirical error margins, rank/thread counts and explicit units. Check measured usage; resource shortage stops or proposes an approved alternative without silently changing the model.
RESOURCE.cons: Predictions need profiling and are not strict universal upper bounds.
RESOURCE.risks: Polynomial formulas omit temporaries, auxiliary basis, rank replication and disk; forced method fallback changes science.

LICENSE.reviewed_requirement: Discover installed version, executable, real license/EULA conditions and administrator authorization. Remove invented ORCA/CFOUR authentication tokens and license-server assumptions; a local manifest records attestation, not legal proof.
LICENSE.pros: Supports legitimate engines and portable installs.
LICENSE.risks: False DRM can block authorized users or falsely assert authorization.

TIER.reviewed_requirement: Represent named method/basis/dispersion/reference/derivative profiles in a capability registry. Tier numbers are organizational labels, not a monotonic accuracy ranking; use one canonical mapping across files.
TIER.risks: Changing tiers, reference states or basis silently invalidates comparisons.

DH.reviewed_requirement: Keep exact open-source revDSD as a gated extension until its SCF functional, spin-resolved MP2 components, coefficients, D3/D4 variants and response gradients match independently validated reference fixtures. Do not assemble ad hoc energy coefficients or promise analytic gradients.
DH.cons: Substantial theory, derivative and cross-engine validation work.
DH.risks: Incorrect coefficient/dispersion/response combinations can produce smooth but wrong PESs.

SYM.reviewed_requirement: Keep tolerance-aware point-group proposals, atom mapping and optional coordinate symmetrization with recorded displacement. Separate geometry constraints, electronic symmetry and spectroscopic symmetry. Validate full-space curvature; symmetry does not guarantee saddle order.
SYM.pros: Reduces numerical ambiguity and supports expert control.
SYM.risks: Forced symmetry can create false stationary points; exact matching on noisy input can miss valid symmetry.

PI.reviewed_requirement: Recognize supported nonrigid models and retain PI metadata, but require feasible permutations, nuclear spin weights, validated torsion-rotation Hamiltonians and reference spectra before general automated PI assignment or tunneling prediction.
PI.cons: Specialist model definitions and solvers are required.
PI.risks: A torsional score or PI flag alone cannot derive correct groups, selection rules or splittings.

PES.reviewed_requirement: Use periodic coordinates, explicit constraints, deterministic seeds, branch identity, relaxed forward/reverse or multi-start coverage and reference anchors. Count integer grid points with only proven symmetry reduction. Treat adaptive sampling as bounded exploration, never global-minimum proof.
PES.pros: Reduces redundant work and scan hysteresis.
PES.risks: Coarse/ML scans can miss narrow wells; dimensionality reduction can omit coupled motion.

TS.reviewed_requirement: Validate optimization tolerances, full projected mass-weighted Hessian and target saddle index: zero significant imaginary modes for minima, one for TS. Validate both IRC endpoints with atom mapping and internal-coordinate/topology checks; log numerical ambiguity.
TS.risks: A one-imaginary-frequency saddle need not connect intended endpoints; fixed RMSD alone is insufficient.

LAM.reviewed_requirement: Add a versioned hindered-rotor/DVR/variational profile only with specified kinetic operator, mass metric, periodicity, coupling, basis/grid convergence, observables and applicability criteria. Preserve VPT2 validity diagnostics; do not switch using a universal barrier/dispersion threshold.
LAM.pros: Can treat motions where perturbation theory is inadequate.
LAM.cons: New solvers and expensive PES/property surfaces.
LAM.risks: A 1D DVR is exact only for its chosen reduced Hamiltonian; omitted coupling can dominate error.

VPT.reviewed_requirement: Separate harmonic ZPE, vibration-rotation constants and effective B0. VPT2 needs supported cubic/semi-diagonal quartic force fields, resonance treatment, mode conventions and convergence checks; a Hessian or frequency scaling alone does not supply general alpha constants.
VPT.pros: Prevents mislabeled equilibrium or approximate values.
VPT.risks: Soft modes and resonances can invalidate perturbative treatment.

SPIN.reviewed_requirement: Report S2 with state/method and absolute-plus-relative policy appropriate to singlets/open shells. Flag diagnostics with context; do not infer exact failure or automatically replace references. Validate SCF stationarity/stability and preserve targeted excited/metastable state identity.
SPIN.risks: Spin projection or RO switching changes the model; T1/D1 alone neither prove nor exclude multireference character.

MR.reviewed_requirement: Require approved active orbitals/electrons, state roots and weights, root tracking, dynamic-correlation method and continuity tests. Automated/ML selection may propose active spaces but cannot silently resolve them.
MR.pros: Supports static correlation beyond single-reference methods.
MR.cons: High computational cost and specialist validation.
MR.risks: Inconsistent active spaces/root flips yield discontinuous surfaces; a lower variational energy is not proof of a better target state.

BSSE.reviewed_requirement: Validate disjoint complete fragment atom maps, charges and multiplicities for CP requests. Keep raw, CP interaction, deformation and binding energies distinct; correct gradients when optimizing a CP PES. Apply correction only to compatible methods; record 3c/dispersion composition to avoid double counting.
BSSE.pros: Makes intermolecular energies and corrections traceable.
BSSE.risks: Universal forced CP/gCP or incompatible composite corrections can worsen results.

ANALYTICS.reviewed_requirement: Retain QTAIM/NCI/ELF and orbital descriptors with raw values, units, method/density provenance, numerical convergence and qualified interpretations. Do not treat BCP or Laplacian/energy-density thresholds as universal bond classification or VPT2 validity proof.
ANALYTICS.cons: Grid convergence and interpretation require care.
ANALYTICS.risks: Topology is not unique evidence of bond energy, dispersion mechanism or dynamics.

NBO.reviewed_requirement: Verify each tool and version actually provides NPA/NAO/NBO/NRT/E2 operations and necessary Fock/density/orbitals; label JANPA-derived descriptors by their actual definition, without claiming identity with proprietary NBO. E2 terms are model-specific perturbative descriptors, not an additive binding-energy decomposition.
NBO.cons: Adapters, licensing and reference validation differ.
NBO.risks: Unsupported capabilities or interchangeable branding can fabricate scientific results.

WFN.reviewed_requirement: Preserve native wavefunctions plus validated converted artifacts with basis coefficients/order/normalization, density type, spin blocks, electron-count trace and orbital overlap checks. HDF5 is a project container, not automatically QCSchema/QCIO or lossless universal Molden.
WFN.risks: Natural/correlated/spinor/ECP wavefunctions are not always representable in a target format.

EXPORT.reviewed_requirement: Use versioned typed output schemas, units/axes/state labels, quality/source tags and authentic parser/round-trip fixtures. Keep observed .lin measurements distinct from predictions; validate Pickett IDs, signs and reductions against its actual manual. Preserve missing/unsupported separately from zero.
EXPORT.cons: Consumer contracts and format variants require tests.
EXPORT.risks: Incorrect parameter IDs, state labels or precision corrupt spectra despite valid text.

PROPS.reviewed_requirement: Export requested available dipoles/EFG/quadrupole/spin-rotation/hyperfine properties with full axes, isotope constants, theory levels and convergence. EFG-to-chi uses nuclear quadrupole moment and units. Mandatory properties depend on target nuclei/state and solver capability.
PROPS.cons: Different properties may need different methods.
PROPS.risks: Dipoles alone do not predict instrumental SNR; unqualified exactness or forced tensor completeness is false.

ISOTOPE.reviewed_requirement: Reuse the Born-Oppenheimer electronic PES for chosen isotope substitutions, rediagonalize inertia and mass-weighted Hessians, rotate all tensors consistently and record abundance/degeneracy. Vibrational corrections, DBOC and populations are isotope-dependent.
ISOTOPE.risks: Mass-only Be is not B0; substitution axes can rotate or become degenerate.

KINETICS.reviewed_requirement: Keep barriers and graph connectivity; add kinetics only in an explicit validated TST/RRKM/tunneling/master-equation profile with temperature, pressure, collisional and timescale assumptions. Do not prune conformers using one universal jet-cooling barrier.
KINETICS.risks: Equilibrium Boltzmann weights or 1D transmission factors do not establish jet populations or line broadening.

UI.reviewed_requirement: Add a CoChem-base view of persisted scientific state with visible assumptions, provenance and keyboard/headless equivalents. Manual edits create a new revision; UI refresh/disconnect cannot mutate or terminate work.
UI.pros: Makes computed results and operator choices inspectable.
UI.risks: UI-only checks cannot enforce backend constraints; display labels must not overclaim validation.

ORCH.reviewed_requirement: Use durable idempotent task state, restartable adapters, bounded retries, leases, cancellation and preserved raw logs/checkpoints; route by declared capability. Existing approval covers bounded batch work. Add framework adapters without mandating a wholesale rewrite.
ORCH.cons: Distributed operations and deployment need validation.
ORCH.risks: Unbounded retries, duplicate jobs, unsafe cleanup or NFS SQLite WAL can lose work or exceed budgets.

DEPLOY.reviewed_requirement: Use pinned reproducible environments and supported local/Slurm/container profiles with license-compliant external binaries. Probe actual CUDA/ROCm/MPI capabilities and keep CPU fallback where scientifically equivalent. Verify distributions and record hardware/software.
DEPLOY.cons: Containers and GPU/MPI portability still require site tests.
DEPLOY.risks: Packaging cannot guarantee drivers, licenses, ABI or target capabilities.

TEST.reviewed_requirement: Separate deterministic unit/contract tests, reference scientific fixtures and real-engine integration/benchmark suites. Report unavailable optional engines explicitly; release requires declared mandatory suites. Use tolerances justified by reference uncertainty and method/domain.
TEST.risks: Banning all test doubles/skips or universal experimental tolerances creates false failures or false coverage.

RESEARCH.reviewed_requirement: Keep as a research extension pending primary-source verification, implementation availability, domain benchmarks and isolated acceptance criteria; do not make an unverified citation or performance claim normative.
RESEARCH.pros: Potential future accuracy or efficiency gain.
RESEARCH.cons: Validation effort and maintenance are unresolved.
RESEARCH.risks: Novel results may not generalize and should not replace converged reference calculations.

REJECT.reviewed_requirement: Remove the stated rule because its claimed implication is scientifically or architecturally invalid; preserve the underlying diagnostic or data where useful without executing the unsupported automatic action.
REJECT.cons: Some proposed automation is deliberately unavailable.
REJECT.risks: Implementing the original rule would silently change scientific conclusions.

PLACEHOLDER.reviewed_requirement: No actionable scientific requirement is supplied. Record the placeholder as reviewed; do not invent the missing twenty suggestions or treat a conversational audit claim as evidence.
PLACEHOLDER.risks: Claiming these were implemented would misrepresent the source.

1: Retain ecosystem boundary and typed contracts; remove unqualified sub-chemical/guaranteed accuracy claims, fabricated DRM, cryptographic misuse, ML and spectral pruning certainty. Explicit metadata, task scope and measurable acceptance are needed.
2: Replace monotonic ladder and conflicting numbering with capability registry; verify actual derivatives/properties and no-license revDSD. Post-HF methods can be less accurate for a given observable than a lower-numbered method.
3: Separate electronic point group, mass/isotopic symmetry and nonrigid PI group. Retain optional constrained symmetry with full-space stability diagnostics; no engine keyword guarantees saddle index. Remove proprietary GPU4SCF assertion pending actual package verification.
4: Define coordinate proposals, atom-matched endpoints, periodic grids, scoped reaction policy, budgets and TS/IRC validation. Safe defaults preserve all inputs and record selections. Geodesic/NEB methods are choices, not guaranteed global-path algorithms.
5: Define bounded adaptive exploration and matched inter-method relative-energy/observable comparisons. Distinguish numerical convergence, method stability and empirical accuracy. Record budget exhausted, maximum profile reached and unresolved coverage separately from success.
6: Minimum validation must reject one imaginary mode, not only more than one. Define optimizers, force/displacement units, external-mode projection and state continuity. DBOC is a diagonal Born-Oppenheimer correction, not a relativistic effect.
7: Require cubic/semi-diagonal quartic force fields and resonance/applicability policy for VPT2. Keep Be/B0 distinct, property axes and full tensors. Ground-state rotational constants cannot be produced from geometry alone; arbitrary 30 versus 100 kcal/mol cutoffs conflict.
8: Correct Watson A: Delta_J/Delta_JK/Delta_K/delta_J/delta_K; S: D_J/D_JK/D_K/d1/d2. Define actual Pickett files, IDs and units with round trips. HDF5 paths cannot simultaneously be dataset and group; Hessian-only VPT2 and automatic covariance claims are false.
9: Validate actual JANPA/NBO capabilities and density conversion. Keep descriptive QTAIM/NCI/ELF interpretation distinct from energies, chemical graph identity and vibration-model validity; document grid errors, correlated density type and tool provenance.
10: Keep CoChem-base UI integration and headless backend; define CLI/API equivalents and prior-approved batch policy. Latest EULA clarification supersedes fabricated tokens. Strong signatures are optional deployment threat-model choices, not a scientific prerequisite.
11: Hardware routing follows engine/property/version capability and allocated resources, not tier or universal CPU/GPU assertions. Correct tblite/GPU assumptions, unverified GPU4SCF naming and SpycFit responsibility. Do not silently migrate unsupported electronic state/checkpoints.
12: Define bounded, state-aware recovery categories and durable outcomes. No forced spin projection, active-space selection or DLPNO substitution without an approved profile. Diagnostics yield qualified warnings; preserve evidence and optional-property failure independently.
13: Define isotope enumeration caps, actual isotope masses/spins/abundances, BO reuse and mass-dependent corrections. Minor isotopologues do not generally dominate all dense spectra. Placeholder twenty suggestions are absent.
14: Define a rapid single-conformer profile with supported engine, derivative route, numerical checks and labeled Be/B0 outputs; no promised 1–2% error. Keep full PES exploration bypass explicit and report absence of conformer coverage. Fifteen standard-processing placeholders contain no requirements.

points.title: Integrate MACE/Equiformer Potentials for Enhanced Pre-Flight Sanitization
points.reason: MACE/Equiformer are optional candidates; architecture choice does not prove better off-equilibrium accuracy.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Integrate MACE/Equiformer Potentials for Enhanced Pre-Flight Sanitization. Rationale: While AIMNet2 is fast, state-of-the-art equivariant message-passing networks like MACE and Equiformer v2 offer superior data efficiency and accuracy for off-equilibrium geometries. Upgrading the sanitization filter to MACE prevents the erroneous rejection of valid, highly-distorted conformers during initial screening. Citation: Batatia, I. et al. (2022). MACE: Higher Order Equivariant Message Passing Neural Networks for Fast and Accurate Force Fields. NeurIPS.

points.title: Implement Graph-Attention Epistemic Uncertainty Quantification
points.reason: Attention weights are not calibrated epistemic uncertainty; test uncertainty methods against held-out data.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Implement Graph-Attention Epistemic Uncertainty Quantification. Rationale: Relying on simple variance across AIMNet2 heads is often poorly calibrated for out-of-distribution molecules. Upgrading this to graph attention-based epistemic uncertainty using Equiformer V2 captures long-range many-body interactions more robustly, ensuring that heavy DLPNO-CCSD(T) compute is triggered only for genuinely complex electronic structures. Citation: Liao, Y. et al. (2023). EquiformerV2: Improved Equivariant Transformer for Scaling to Higher-Degree Representations. ICLR.

points.title: Mandate AiiDA or Parsl for the Cryptographic Budget Contract
points.reason: AiiDA/Parsl can implement state/provenance; neither a hash nor a framework mathematically enforces all workflow properties.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Mandate AiiDA or Parsl for the Cryptographic Budget Contract. Rationale: A SHA-256 token proves operator authorization but does not maintain workflow state. Integrating a dedicated computational chemistry orchestrator like AiiDA or Parsl ensures the contract mathematically enforces directed acyclic graph (DAG) state, SWEBOK-compliant fault tolerance, and full W3C PROV-O provenance tracking across HPC nodes. Citation: Huber, S. P. et al. (2020). AiiDA 1.0, a scalable computational infrastructure for automated reproducible workflows and data provenance. Scientific Data, 7(1), 300.

points.title: Add ML-Accelerated Pre-Flight Multireference Diagnostics
points.reason: ML static-correlation prediction is a screening warning, never a replacement for diagnostics and state analysis.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Add ML-Accelerated Pre-Flight Multireference Diagnostics. Rationale: Relying exclusively on Coupled-Cluster T1/D1 diagnostics means discovering a multireference breakdown after launching an expensive O(N^6) operation. Integrating an ML model trained to predict static correlation indices from cheap initial DFT densities intercepts multireference systems pre-flight. Citation: Matveeva, A. et al. (2023). Machine learning models for the prediction of multireference character. Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics, 25(11), 8089-8101.

points.title: Utilize ML Potentials for Mapping Large Amplitude Motions (LAMs)
points.reason: ML PES acceleration needs reference anchors and a defined variational solver.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Utilize ML Potentials for Mapping Large Amplitude Motions (LAMs). Rationale: Standard Vibrational Perturbation Theory (VPT2) breaks down completely for LAMs. The specification must define the use of ML potentials (like ANI-2x or MACE) to rapidly map the full 2D/3D torsional potential energy surface prior to solving the vibrational Schrödinger equation, bypassing the catastrophic scaling of ab initio grid scans. Citation: Meuwly, M. (2021). Machine Learning for Chemical Reactions and Molecular Spectroscopy. Chemical Reviews, 121(16), 10218-10239.

points.title: Integrate Algorithmic Active Space Selection (autoCAS)
points.reason: autoCAS proposes a candidate active space; orbital/root continuity and expert review remain necessary.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Integrate Algorithmic Active Space Selection (autoCAS). Rationale: When the "Multireference CC Breakdown" trap fires, halting the pipeline leaves the operator guessing the CASSCF active space. The architecture must mandate an automated orbital entanglement analysis (e.g., DMRG-based autoCAS) to mathematically define the active space, augmenting rather than interrupting the HITL paradigm. Citation: Stein, C. J., & Reiher, M. (2016). Automated selection of active orbital spaces. Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation, 12(4), 1760-1771.

points.title: Require Explicit Dispersion Corrections in ML Gating
points.reason: Do not add D3/D4 to every ML potential: it can double-count training/reference dispersion.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Require Explicit Dispersion Corrections in ML Gating. Rationale: If AIMNet2 is retained over newer equivariant models, the specification must explicitly mandate the use of post-hoc dispersion corrections (e.g., D3(BJ) or D4) during the energy gate. Without explicit dispersion modeling, valid non-covalent dimers will be erroneously flagged as having "severe steric clashes." Citation: Grimme, S. et al. (2016). A robust and accurate non-covalent interaction machine learning potential. The Journal of Chemical Physics, 145(13).

points.title: Mandate Vibrational Averaging for Dipole & Quadrupole Tensors
points.reason: Support vibrationally averaged property surfaces as an explicit accuracy profile, keeping equilibrium values labeled.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Mandate Vibrational Averaging for Dipole & Quadrupole Tensors. Rationale: The contract intelligently requests zero-point (A_0) rotational constants but neglects vibrational averaging for dipoles. Because CP-FTMW intensities scale quadratically with the dipole, providing un-averaged equilibrium dipoles causes significant simulated intensity errors for highly flexible systems. Citation: Puzzarini, C., & Barone, V. (2020). The challenging route to a predictive computational spectroscopy. International Journal of Quantum Chemistry, 120(10).

points.title: Require Conformational Cooling Transition State (TS) Barrier Computations
points.reason: Jet cooling requires kinetic/experimental modeling; low barriers alone cannot justify deletion.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Require Conformational Cooling Transition State (TS) Barrier Computations. Rationale: In CP-FTMW experiments utilizing supersonic expansions, conformers separated by low energy barriers rapidly interconvert to the global minimum. TORQ must automatically compute TS barriers between low-energy wells. Conformers below the barrier threshold must be algorithmically pruned, as they will not be observed experimentally. Citation: Godfrey, P. D., Brown, R. D., & Hunter, F. M. (1998). The shape of molecules: Conformational relaxation in supersonic beams. Journal of Molecular Structure, 417(1-3), 57-73.

points.title: Define Explicit Quantitative QTAIM Classifications
points.reason: Publish descriptor criteria with applicability; universal covalent/dispersion labels are unsupported.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Define Explicit Quantitative QTAIM Classifications. Rationale: Stating QTAIM parameters are "algorithmically evaluated" is architecturally ambiguous. The document must define exact topological thresholds—e.g., requiring Laplacian > 0 and Energy Density < 0 for partial covalent bonds, and both > 0 for purely closed-shell dispersion—to ensure reproducible programmatic classifications. Citation: Macchi, P. et al. (1998). Topological analysis of electron density in chemical bonds. Journal of the American Chemical Society, 120(51), 13402-13414.

points.title: Implement Continuous Chiral Inversion Monitoring During Optimization
points.reason: Monitor declared protected stereocenters during optimization; allowed amine inversion is not automatically corruption.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Implement Continuous Chiral Inversion Monitoring During Optimization. Rationale: Graph invariance is currently only checked at ingestion. High-energy conformers can undergo stereoinversion (e.g., amine umbrella flipping) during the quantum optimization cycle itself. The architecture must require periodic structural graph audits throughout the optimization loop to prevent silent state changes. Citation: Ebejer, J. P. et al. (2012). Freely available conformer generation methods: how good are they? Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling, 52(5), 1146-1158.

points.title: Automate Complete Basis Set (CBS) Extrapolation for High-Frequency Regimes
points.reason: Frequency band alone cannot require CBS, and extrapolation does not mathematically eliminate all basis error.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Automate Complete Basis Set (CBS) Extrapolation for High-Frequency Regimes. Rationale: When predicting mmWave spectra (75-110 GHz), achieving the mandated high accuracy is physically impossible with individual basis sets. The system must automatically trigger a 2-point or 3-point basis set extrapolation workflow (e.g., cc-pVTZ/cc-pVQZ) to mathematically eliminate truncation errors. Citation: Halkier, A. et al. (1998). Basis-set convergence in correlated calculations on Ne, N2, and H2O. Chemical Physics Letters, 286(3-4), 243-252.

points.title: Require HDF5-Backed Serialization for Wavefunction Handoffs
points.reason: Use binary arrays for large data while preserving required native/ASCII adapters; QCArchive is not an HDF5 format guarantee.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Require HDF5-Backed Serialization for Wavefunction Handoffs. Rationale: While QCElemental (JSON) is fine for geometries, passing dense O(N_{bas}^2) matrices (densities, integrals) to tools like Multiwfn via JSON causes massive memory serialization overhead. Mandating an HDF5-backed schema like QCFractal/QCArchive for wavefunction data ensures efficient binary handoffs. Citation: Smith, D. G. et al. (2021). QCArchive: A platform for large-scale quantum chemistry. WIREs Computational Molecular Science, 11(2), e1491.

points.title: Inject Automated BS-DFT Remediation for Spin Contamination
points.reason: Automatic BS-DFT/Yamaguchi correction changes the model; require approved applicability and derivative validation.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Inject Automated BS-DFT Remediation for Spin Contamination. Rationale: Halting a sweep due to spin contamination breaks orchestration automation. The system should instead dynamically route the job to a Broken-Symmetry DFT (BS-DFT) pathway using the Yamaguchi spin-projection formula to algorithmically correct the energy of contaminated open-shell states. Citation: Yamaguchi, K. et al. (1988). A spin correction procedure for unrestricted Hartree-Fock and Møller-Plesset wavefunctions. Chemical Physics Letters, 149(5-6), 537-542.

points.title: Require Formal Uncertainty Propagation for Spectroscopic Constants
points.reason: Do not propagate early ML variance and a functional MAE as though they were independent final-observable error sources.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Require Formal Uncertainty Propagation for Spectroscopic Constants. Rationale: Experimentalists require quantitative error bounds to assign spectra confidently. TORQ must algorithmically propagate the epistemic variance from the initial ML gating and the known statistical Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of the chosen DFT/CC functional into explicit confidence intervals for SpycFit. Citation: Pernot, P. (2017). The statistical setup for the validation of quantum chemistry methods. The Journal of Chemical Physics, 147(15).

points.title: Mandate Density Fitting (RI/COSX) Fallbacks Before Basis Downscaling
points.reason: RI/COSX may reduce cost within validated profile; it is not universal or zero-error CC memory remediation.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Mandate Density Fitting (RI/COSX) Fallbacks Before Basis Downscaling. Rationale: Downscaling a basis set to save memory fundamentally degrades spectroscopic accuracy. Before triggering a downscale, the gatekeeper must automatically inject Resolution of Identity (RI-J/RI-JK) or Chain-of-Spheres (COSX) density fitting approximations, which drastically reduce memory overhead with near-zero accuracy loss. Citation: Neese, F. et al. (2009). Efficient, approximate and parallel Hartree–Fock and hybrid DFT calculations. A ‘chain-of-spheres’ algorithm. Chemical Physics, 356(1-3), 98-109.

points.title: Enforce Core-Valence Correlation for Heavy-Atom Quadrupole Tensors
points.reason: Benchmark core-valence and relativistic sensitivity of heavy-atom EFG; reject a universal basis/core prescription.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Enforce Core-Valence Correlation for Heavy-Atom Quadrupole Tensors. Rationale: Section 1.6.1 mandates Nuclear Quadrupole Coupling Tensors for nuclei like Br and Cl. Standard frozen-core approximations systematically underestimate these tensors because deep core polarization is neglected. The contract must mandate the use of core-valence basis sets (e.g., aug-cc-pCVTZ) and explicitly correlate core electrons when computing quadrupole tensors for heavy halogens. Citation: Puzzarini, C., Heckert, M., & Gauss, J. (2008). The accuracy of rotational constants predicted by high-level quantum-chemical calculations. The Journal of Chemical Physics, 128(19), 194108.

points.title: Automate Heavy-Atom Isotopic Substitution Tensors
points.reason: Bound selected isotopes and abundances; parent geometry gives mass-only equilibrium predictions.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Automate Heavy-Atom Isotopic Substitution Tensors. Rationale: Resolving 3D coordinates in SpycFit relies on Kraitchman analysis of isotopologues. The contract must mandate that TORQ automatically computes and appends the rotational constants and dipole tensors for all natural heavy-atom isotopic substitutions (e.g., 13C, 15N, 18O, 37Cl) from the parent geometry. Citation: Kraitchman, J. (1953). Determination of molecular structure from microwave spectroscopic data. American Journal of Physics, 21(1), 17-24.

points.title: Utilize Unsupervised Clustering (HDBSCAN) for Torsional Sub-Manifolds
points.reason: HDBSCAN can cluster periodic features; it does not guarantee representative coverage or retain narrow wells.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Utilize Unsupervised Clustering (HDBSCAN) for Torsional Sub-Manifolds. Rationale: Attempting "sub-manifold decomposition" using naive grid pruning risks skipping narrow conformational wells. Explicitly requiring density-based unsupervised clustering (e.g., HDBSCAN) on the dihedral feature space ensures mathematically representative, non-redundant sampling of the hyperspace. Citation: Campello, R. J. et al. (2013). Density-based clustering based on hierarchical density estimates. Pacific-Asia Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining.

points.title: Require Quartic Centrifugal Distortion Constants
points.reason: Require quartic distortion in a supported high-J profile; record Watson conventions and harmonic-force-field derivation.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** Require Quartic Centrifugal Distortion Constants. Rationale: Section 1.6.1 currently only requests rigid rotational constants. For high-resolution CP-FTMW extending to higher J transitions, the inclusion of Quartic Centrifugal Distortion Constants (e.g., D_J, D_JK, d_1 in Watson's A or S reduction) computed via analytic second derivatives is strictly required for spectral assignment. Citation: Watson, J. K. G. (1977). Aspects of quartic and sextic centrifugal distortion on rotational energy levels. Vibrational Spectra and Structure, 6, 1-89.

points.title: Integration of LLM-Agentic Diagnostics for Failed TS Searches
points.reason: LLM TS diagnostics add nondeterminism and unverified 99.9% convergence claims; use bounded deterministic recovery first.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 1. Integration of LLM-Agentic Diagnostics for Failed TS Searches
Action: Implement an agentic plan-execute-analyze replanning loop (e.g., utilizing TSAgent protocols) within TORQ to autonomously adjust TS search parameters (step size, trust radius, Hessian update scheme) when quasi-Newton methods fail to converge.
Rationale: Transition state optimizations are notoriously fragile. Static heuristics often fail, whereas LLM-guided/agentic workflows achieve near 99.9% convergence on complex benchmarks like Transition1X.
Citation: "LLM-Driven Evolution of Transition State Search Workflows" and "TSAgent: Automated Transition State Search at the Density Functional Theory Level" (arXiv 2026).

points.title: Geodesic Interpolation for Initial Minimum Energy Path (MEP) Guesses
points.reason: Geodesic initialization is an available strategy, not a clash-free mathematical guarantee or universal mandatory algorithm.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 2. Geodesic Interpolation for Initial Minimum Energy Path (MEP) Guesses
Action: Replace Linear Synchronous Transit (LST) or basic internal coordinate interpolation with Geodesic Interpolation in Delocalized Internal Coordinates (DLC) as the mandatory method for generating the initial connecting string between TOPOS isomers.
Rationale: Geodesic interpolation mathematically avoids unphysical steric clashes and atom tangling commonly seen in large-amplitude isomerizations, drastically reducing the number of gradients required for subsequent string convergence.
Citation: Xia, X., et al., "Improved String Methods and Geodesic Interpolation for PES Mapping."

points.title: Mandate Double-Ended String Methods (CI-DNEB/GSM) for Pathway Mapping
points.reason: Double-ended NEB/GSM is appropriate with matched endpoints; retain supported alternatives and genuine single-ended searches.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 3. Mandate Double-Ended String Methods (CI-DNEB/GSM) for Pathway Mapping
Action: Require the use of the Growing String Method (GSM) or Climbing Image Dynamic Nudged Elastic Band (CI-DNEB) rather than single-ended eigenvector-following for all isomer pairs provided by TOPOS.
Rationale: Since TOPOS explicitly provides the reactant and product endpoints, double-ended string methods are significantly more physically robust, computationally efficient, and less prone to "walking off" the PES compared to single-ended searches.
Citation: Recent reviews on automated reaction pathway exploration (e.g., J. Chem. Phys. standard NEB literature and ARplorer 2025).

points.title: AIMNet2-Preconditioned String Relaxation
points.reason: ML string relaxation must be optional for models that cover the pathway chemistry.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 4. AIMNet2-Preconditioned String Relaxation
Action: Before expending high-level DFT or CCSD(T) budget on the string nodes, mandate a complete MEP pre-relaxation utilizing the GPU-accelerated AIMNet2 engine.
Rationale: This perfectly aligns with Chapter 1's use of AIMNet2 for pre-flight sanitization. Pre-optimizing the string with AIMNet2 minimizes the calculation budget needed for the final ab initio TS refinement.
Citation: ML Potentials in TS Searches (2024/2025 literature on NNP-accelerated NEB and GSM).

points.title: Automated Intermediates Branching (String Cleavage Trap)
points.reason: Validate candidate intermediate minima then branch with deduplication and remaining-budget checks.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 5. Automated Intermediates Branching (String Cleavage Trap)
Action: If a GSM/NEB string collapses into a stable intermediate well rather than locating a single TS, trigger an automated `StringCleavageTrap` to bifurcate the job into two new independent string searches connecting to the intermediate.
Rationale: Prevents complete job failure due to hidden stable intermediates in complex, multi-step isomer interchanges.
Citation: Zimmerman, P. M., "Growing string method with interpolation and optimization" (J. Comput. Chem.) and ARplorer pathway methodologies.

points.title: Interactive PesLandscapeWidget for HITL Steering
points.reason: Persist node edits and provenance; UI steering must submit a new approved plan revision.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 6. Interactive PesLandscapeWidget for HITL Steering
Action: Expand the Voila GUI suite with a `PesLandscapeWidget` that provides 2D/3D contour plotting of relaxed torsional scans and string methods, allowing the spectroscopist to interactively view the profile, manipulate nodes, and authorize TS optimization.
Rationale: Preserves the PMBOK/SWEBOK mandated Human-In-The-Loop (HITL) philosophy for resource-intensive operations, directly analogous to the existing `ToposEnsembleInspectorWidget`.
Citation: Visual analytics best practices for computational chemistry and interactive quantum mechanics workflows.

points.title: VRI (Valley-Ridge Inflection) Point Detection Trap
points.reason: A negative second Hessian eigenvalue alone is not a VRI definition; projected curvature and gradient conditions are required.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 7. VRI (Valley-Ridge Inflection) Point Detection Trap
Action: Implement an algorithmic trap during the Intrinsic Reaction Coordinate (IRC) descent to compute the second lowest Hessian eigenvalue. If it becomes negative, flag the bifurcating surface (VRI point) and halt downstream dispatch.
Rationale: Bifurcations indicate that a single TS connects to more than two minima. Ignoring VRIs leads to incorrect isomer interchange assignments in SpycFit kinetic networks.
Citation: Quapp, W. et al., "Valley-ridge inflection points...", Theor. Chem. Acc.

points.title: Strict IRC Endpoint Verification Contract
points.reason: Verify mapped IRC endpoints with adaptive tolerances; cryptographic integrity does not validate the physics.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 8. Strict IRC Endpoint Verification Contract
Action: Require a cryptographic validation step where the mass-weighted IRC descent from the optimized TS must geometrically converge to the original TOPOS-supplied isomers with a heavy-atom RMSD < 0.15 Å.
Rationale: Ensures that the TS physically connects the intended isomers, preventing "TS hopping" where the optimizer inadvertently wanders to a completely different reaction pathway.
Citation: Fukui's formulation of the Intrinsic Reaction Coordinate and standard SOPs for automated reaction discovery.

points.title: Dynamic Grid Slicing via PCA for High Torsional Complexity
points.reason: Ordinary PCA on wrapped angles is invalid; use periodic features and validate omitted-coupling error.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 9. Dynamic Grid Slicing via PCA for High Torsional Complexity
Action: When C_torsion exceeds 1000 (from Section 1.4.4), do not immediately block the job. Instead, perform Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on the torsional covariance matrix to slice the grid into the 2-3 most coupled dihedrals.
Rationale: Prevents rigid execution blocks and allows complex multi-rotor isomerizations to proceed gracefully by algorithmically reducing dimensionality, maximizing the utility of the CalculationBudgetContract.
Citation: Dimensionality reduction techniques in PES exploration and metadynamics literature.

points.title: Tighter Multireference Breakdown Thresholds at TS Geometry
points.reason: No evidence supports universal stricter TS-specific T1=0.015/D1=0.04 cutoffs.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 10. Tighter Multireference Breakdown Thresholds at TS Geometry
Action: Override the equilibrium T1 > 0.02 / D1 > 0.05 diagnostic trap to a stricter threshold (e.g., T1 > 0.015 or D1 > 0.04) exclusively at the Transition State geometry.
Rationale: Transition states inherently feature stretched bonds and significant static correlation. A tighter threshold ensures multi-reference character is flagged before calculating extremely expensive CCSD(T) gradients on an invalid wavefunction.
Citation: Lee, T. J., Taylor, P. R., "A diagnostic for determining the quality of single-reference electron correlation methods".

points.title: Wigner-Eckart Tunneling Coefficient Injection
points.reason: Wigner correction and Eckart barrier transmission are separate approximations; Wigner-Eckart is an unrelated theorem.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 11. Wigner-Eckart Tunneling Coefficient Injection
Action: For hydrogen-transfer tautomerizations or light-atom isomerizations, calculate 1D Wigner or Eckart tunneling transmission probabilities using the TS imaginary frequency and append this data to the SpycFit spectroscopic contract.
Rationale: Tunneling significantly accelerates isomer interchange rates at low temperatures (critical for interstellar CP-FTMW observations). Purely classical barrier heights are insufficient for accurate modeling.
Citation: Truhlar, D. G. et al., Variational Transition State Theory with Multidimensional Tunneling (VTST/MT).

points.title: 1D-DVR for Large Amplitude Low-Barrier Torsions
points.reason: A 2 kcal/mol threshold cannot establish 1D decoupling; DVR is not exact full-molecular dynamics.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 12. 1D-DVR for Large Amplitude Low-Barrier Torsions
Action: If the TS barrier for an isomer interchange is < 2.0 kcal/mol, bypass standard harmonic VPT2 zero-point corrections and automatically trigger a 1D Discrete Variable Representation (1D-DVR) solver along the isomerization mode.
Rationale: Harmonic approximations fail catastrophically for shallow torsional wells. 1D-DVR provides exact quantum torsional energy levels, which are absolutely required for scaling the A0, B0, C0 constants correctly.
Citation: Meyer, R., "Internal rotation and torsion...", generalized DVR literature for large amplitude molecular motions.

points.title: Local Active Space Retraining (Active Learning NNP)
points.reason: Active learning needs held-out error/force checks, budgets and reference anchors; it does not bypass validation.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 13. Local Active Space Retraining (Active Learning NNP)
Action: For large-amplitude conformation spaces where AIMNet2 epistemic uncertainty is high (σ_E >= 0.50 kcal/mol), implement an Active Learning loop to train a localized Neural Network Potential over the specific PES using batched, lightweight DFT.
Rationale: Solves the problem of high epistemic uncertainty by adaptively refining the ML surrogate on-the-fly, completely bypassing the need to map the full grid with expensive ab initio methods.
Citation: Behler-Parrinello NNP Active Learning literature and 2024/2025 ML-PES generation frameworks.

points.title: Conical Intersection (CI) & State-Averaged PES Checks
points.reason: Ground-state AIMNet2/DFT cannot provide S1-S0 gaps; excited-state/conical-intersection work is separate scope.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 14. Conical Intersection (CI) & State-Averaged PES Checks
Action: If the initial AIMNet2/DFT MEP scan identifies an S1 - S0 energy gap < 0.5 eV, halt the ground-state string method and trigger a State-Averaged CASSCF or ML-Photodynamics trap to search for a conical intersection.
Rationale: Many isomerizations (e.g., cis-trans) proceed non-adiabatically. Treating them strictly on the ground-state Born-Oppenheimer surface will yield entirely unphysical energy barriers and spectral dynamics.
Citation: Recent advancements in ML-accelerated photodynamics and non-adiabatic TS localization (2025/2026).

points.title: Pre-Flight Steric Alignment (Orienta Integration)
points.reason: Use atom-mapped rigid alignment and steric-aware interpolation; Orienta citation/tool remains unverified.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 15. Pre-Flight Steric Alignment (Orienta Integration)
Action: Implement a VSEPR-inspired steric minimization pre-flight orientation algorithm (analogous to the Orienta toolkit) to optimally align the two TOPOS-supplied isomers in Cartesian space prior to generating the string.
Rationale: Poor Cartesian spatial alignment of the endpoints causes string methods to artificially break bonds or unnecessarily rotate the entire molecule, wasting valuable quantum gradients on meaningless coordinate translations.
Citation: "Orienta" (2026) – Automated reactant/product orientation for double-ended TS searches.

points.title: Isotopologue-Invariant TS Mapping
points.reason: Reuse electronic stationary points under BO, but recompute mass-dependent quantities per isotopologue.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 16. Isotopologue-Invariant TS Mapping
Action: Enforce that the PES setup intrinsically evaluates mass-dependent properties (reduced mass, harmonic frequencies) for all isotopic permutations simultaneously at the stationary points, rather than requiring separate PES sweeps.
Rationale: The electronic PES is invariant to isotopic substitution under the Born-Oppenheimer approximation. Extracting all isotopologue data from a single high-level PES sweep maximizes resource efficiency and satisfies SpycFit's isotopic blueprint requirements.
Citation: Standard Born-Oppenheimer principles and high-resolution spectroscopic isotopic substitution theories.

points.title: Projected ZPE Corrections along the MEP
points.reason: Project external modes and path tangent consistently; projection does not guarantee all transverse curvatures are positive.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 17. Projected ZPE Corrections along the MEP
Action: When computing Zero-Point Energies along the string to correct barrier heights, mandate that the reaction path tangent vector is mathematically projected out of the Hessian before the frequency analysis.
Rationale: Standard frequency calculations at non-stationary points yield imaginary frequencies orthogonal to the path. Projecting the tangent ensures stable, real harmonic frequencies, preventing imaginary contamination in the ZPE.
Citation: Miller, W. H., et al., Reaction Path Hamiltonian methods.

points.title: Fractional Dispersion Conservation Traps (QTAIM at TS)
points.reason: BCPs can appear/disappear physically; their conservation cannot validate a TS or forbid dissociation.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 18. Fractional Dispersion Conservation Traps (QTAIM at TS)
Action: For non-covalent isomer interchanges, mandate an automated QTAIM analysis (via Multiwfn) at the TS to verify that Bond Critical Points (BCPs) of key dispersion interactions are not unphysically severed.
Rationale: Directly aligns with Chapter 1's QTAIM assessments. Optimizers often tear apart weakly bound complexes at the TS. Validating BCPs ensures the TS represents an actual conformational rearrangement rather than a dissociation artifact.
Citation: Bader, R. F. W., "Atoms in Molecules" and QTAIM-based TS validation studies.

points.title: RRKM / TST Kinetic Rate Constant Export
points.reason: Kinetic rate export is optional and model-dependent; RRKM is microcanonical before thermal averaging.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 19. RRKM / TST Kinetic Rate Constant Export
Action: Require TORQ to export temperature-dependent Rice-Ramsperger-Kassel-Marcus (RRKM) or standard Transition State Theory (TST) rate constants k(T) alongside the SpycFit physical parameter deliverable.
Rationale: Microwave spectroscopists heavily rely on kinetic rates to determine if an isomer interchange is fast on the experimental timescale, which directly causes spectral line broadening, splitting, or coalescence in the observed spectra.
Citation: Steinfeld, J. I., et al., "Chemical Kinetics and Dynamics" (RRKM theory).

points.title: Dynamic Hessian Routing for Missing Analytical Engines
points.reason: Finite-difference Hessians require verified energies/gradients, step-size tests, symmetry and explicit cost reservation.
points.source_text:
- [ ] **Improver:** 20. Dynamic Hessian Routing for Missing Analytical Engines
Action: Implement an algorithmic fallback that intercepts TS searches on engines lacking analytical Hessians for the requested functional (e.g., double-hybrid revDSD in ORCA) and reroutes the calculation to use semi-numerical Hessians while debiting the CalculationBudgetContract.
Rationale: TS optimization requires precise Hessians. A hard crash due to missing analytical gradients breaks the automated pipeline. Proactive semi-numerical rerouting ensures strict SWEBOK compliance and uninterrupted execution.
Citation: Quantum chemistry software architecture best practices (e.g., ORCA and PySCF manual guidelines on numerical differentiation).

points.title: Time-Series Early Warning System for SCF Non-Convergence

points.source_text: - [ ] **Improver:** 1. Time-Series Early Warning System for SCF Non-Convergence: Update Chapter 12 to treat SCF iterations as a time-series problem. Introduce a gradient-boosted classifier that analyzes the first 10 SCF steps to predict impending failure and trigger an early halt to save compute hours under the CalculationBudgetContract. Rationale: Prevents wasting GPU/CPU cycles on doomed trajectories, allowing faster redirection. Citation: Dong, L., et al. (2026). Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation. DOI: 10.1021/acs.jctc.6c00928

Rationale: Converts the static SWEBOK Gatekeeper into a dynamic, hardware-aware load balancer that strictly enforces cryptographic wall-time budgets. Citation: Safari, M., et al. (2026). Proceedings of the 23rd ACM International Conference on Computing Frontiers. DOI: 10.1145/3801488.3806380

Rationale & Citation: Zubatyuk et al. (Chem. Sci., 2025, 16, 10228–10244) demonstrated that AIMNet2 evaluates thousands of conformer energies per second on CUDA GPUs while capturing long-range electrostatics, allowing high-throughput pre-clearing of unphysical geometries to protect expensive downstream ab initio queues.

points.title: Uncertainty-Gated Boundary Contract for Autonomous Computational Budget Allocation
points.reason: Ensemble disagreement requires calibration; define intermediate 0.15–0.50 and unavailable-model behavior.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Cycle 2:** 2. Uncertainty-Gated Boundary Contract for Autonomous Computational Budget Allocation: Update Section 1.2 to define a quantitative computational budget allocation metric based on AIMNet2 deep ensemble variance (\sigma_E). If the ensemble standard deviation across the 4 neural network heads satisfies \sigma_E < 0.15 kcal/mol, TORQ assigns a lightweight cascade terminating at Tier 4/5 DFT; if \sigma_E >= 0.50 kcal/mol (indicating high epistemic uncertainty in rare torsional configurations), TORQ automatically escalates the computational budget and tags the geometry for high-level wave-function refinement. Rationale & Citation: Ensemble disagreement in MLFFs directly reflects epistemic model error (Zubatyuk et al., ChemRxiv 2024; Batatia et al., MACE-OFF23, 2023). Utilizing \sigma_E as a formal boundary condition ensures computational hours are concentrated strictly where empirical/ML models exhibit low confidence.

points.source_text:
- [ ] **Cycle 7:** Suggestion 1: Physical Validation Gate for Upstream Conformer Ingestion Using Ground-State Rotational Constants (A0, B0, C0) Error Tolerances.
Actionable Recommendation: Establish a strict acceptance gate at the CoChem-TORQ ingestion boundary for 3D conformer candidates generated by upstream modules (CoChem-TOPOS / GOAT / CREST). Before dispatching computationally intensive stationary point optimizations or ab initio PES mapping, evaluate initial rotational constants (Ae, Be, Ce) computed via fast MLFF/GFN2-xTB against empirical microwave detection bounds, rejecting or penalizing conformers whose effective rotational constant Beff deviates by >1.5% from expected structural benchmarks.
Rationale & Citation: In broadband chirped-pulse Fourier transform microwave (CP-FTMW) spectroscopy, spectral assignment algorithms (e.g., AUTOFIT) require initial rotational constant guesses within 1–2% to prevent combinatorial assignment failure and false positives in peak matching (Pate et al., Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys., 2011, 13, 2198-2207; Neill et al., J. Mol. Spectrosc., 2012, 280, 42-50). Establishing this boundary validation eliminates downstream wasted compute cycles on unviable conformers.

points.source_text:
- [ ] **Cycle 7:** Suggestion 2: Rigorous Boundary Contract Specifying Dipole Components and Quadrupole Coupling Tensors as Mandatory Deliverables.
Actionable Recommendation: Formally update Chapter 1 boundary deliverables to require that TORQ ingest and deliver full electric dipole moment vectors (mu_a, mu_b, mu_c) and nuclear quadrupole coupling tensors (chi_aa, chi_bb, chi_cc, chi_ab) alongside rotational constants into all downstream artifacts.
Rationale & Citation: In rotational spectroscopy, transition intensities scale quadratically with dipole moment components (I ~ mu_alpha^2 * nu^2), meaning rotational constants alone are incapable of synthesizing observable spectra or predicting experimental signal-to-noise ratios in CP-FTMW instruments (Gordy & Cook, Microwave Molecular Spectra, 3rd ed., Wiley, 1984; Puzzarini et al., Chem. Rev., 2019, 119, 8131-8191). Incorporating dipole vectors and quadrupole coupling tensors at the boundary level ensures physical completeness across the pipeline.

points.source_text: - [ ] **Cycle 10:** Upstream-to-Downstream Electronic State Contract & Spin Expectation Trap: In cochem_torq.preprocessor, implement a strict Pydantic/dataclass schema contract for incoming topologies from CoChem-TOPOS that mandates explicit charge, target spin multiplicity (2S+1), and calculated expectation value <S^2>. If an unrestricted calculation deviates such that Δ<S^2> = |<S^2> - S(S+1)| > 0.10 * S(S+1) (or > 0.05 for open-shell doublets/triplets), TORQ must immediately halt execution, block downstream PES escalation, and flag the state as spin-contaminated. Rationale: Unrestricted Hartree-Fock and Kohn-Sham determinants for open-shell systems frequently suffer from artificial high-spin state contamination, introducing severe non-physical energetic biases and unphysical geometry distortions into downstream PES scans. (Citations: Yamaguchi et al., Chem. Phys. Lett. 1986, 133, 34–38; Method Matrix v4.2, Section 12.5).

points.source_text: - [ ] **Cycle 10:** Boundary Contract for Topological Fragment Demarcation in Boys-Bernardi BSSE Tracking: Define an explicit structural interface between CoChem-TOPOS and CoChem-TORQ for non-covalent complexes (5–10 atoms) requiring fragment indices (fragment_A_indices, fragment_B_indices) for all non-covalent adducts. TORQ must enforce this contract before accepting any dimer geometry: if fragments are undefined or overlapping, TORQ must reject the job rather than attempting uncorrected single-molecule optimizations, enabling automated ghost-atom assignment (using ORCA ghost syntax ':' or PySCF ghost bases) for standard Boys-Bernardi counterpoise corrections. Rationale: Without unambiguous upstream fragment assignment, automated pipelines cannot construct the ghost-atom basis partitions required for standard Counterpoise corrections, silently leading to BSSE-induced artificial contraction of intermolecular distances by 4–9 pm. (Citations: Boys & Bernardi, Mol. Phys. 1970, 19, 553–566; Plumley & Dannenberg, J. Comput. Chem. 2011, 32, 1519–1527).

points.reason: T1/D1 are diagnostic evidence, not an emergency proof of single-reference collapse.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Cycle 10:** Multireference Diagnostic Gate Trapping Coupled-Cluster Breakdown (T1/D1 Diagnostics): Establish a strict pre-dispatch boundary check in TORQ's execution manager that evaluates the single-excitation amplitude norm (T1) and matrix 2-norm (D1) from preliminary coupled-cluster runs or CCSD scouts. If T1 > 0.020 (for closed-shell organics) or T1 > 0.045 (for open-shell radicals), or D1 > 0.050, the system must trip an emergency boundary quarantine, aborting single-reference CCSD(T) escalations and issuing an alert that the stationary point exhibits severe static correlation requiring multireference methods. Rationale: Blindly pushing open-shell or diradicaloid complexes into single-reference CCSD(T) or DLPNO-CCSD(T) when T1/D1 diagnostics are violated produces disastrous non-variational energy collapse and corrupted force fields. (Citations: Lee & Taylor, Int. J. Quantum Chem. 1989, 36, 199–207; Janssen & Nielsen, Chem. Phys. Lett. 1998, 290, 423–430).

Tier 1 Specification: Native PyTorch Integration of AIMNet2 and MACE-OFF23 as Dual-Engine Tier 1 MLFFs: Explicitly define Tier 1 in Section 2.1 as a dual-engine MLFF layer incorporating AIMNet2 (aimnetcentral) and MACE-OFF23 (mace-torch) within an ASE (ase.calculators) wrapper. TORQ must provide automated model selection: default to AIMNet2 for molecules with diverse heteroatoms (including B, Si, P, As, Se, halogens) and charged/zwitterionic states, and fallback to MACE-OFF23 for dense organic/biomolecular torsional networks. Rationale & Citation: Benchmarks on TorsionNet-500 and QC Torsion Drive (Dral et al., JCTC 2024; Batatia et al., 2023; Zubatyuk et al., 2025) demonstrate that AIMNet2 and MACE-OFF23 achieve state-of-the-art accuracy with mean torsional barrier errors below 0.3 kcal/mol, providing an optimal foundation for Tier 1.

The batch size for multi-conformer or multi-point PES scans must dynamically scale according to free VRAM (B = floor(V_free / (M_atom * S_buffer))), preventing CUDA Out-Of-Memory (OOM) faults during heavy PES grid evaluations. Rationale & Citation: Uncontrolled tensor allocation across large conformer batches crashes headless GPU runners. Explicit batch scaling and stream isolation conform to the CoChem Anti-Spoofing Protocol and hardware guardrails.

- [ ] **Cycle 7:** Suggestion 3: Implementation of the 'Cheap-Composite' (junChS) Protocol for Ground-State Rotational Constants (B0) in Tiers 8–10.
Actionable Recommendation: Standardize a 'cheap-composite' scheme (junChS) within TORQ's Method Matrix: evaluate equilibrium rotational constants Be at the CCSD(T)/CBS limit (using a two-point Helgaker X^-3 extrapolation with jun-cc-pVTZ and jun-cc-pVQZ), and combine them with zero-point vibrational corrections (Delta B_vib = -0.5 * sum_i d_i * alpha_i) computed via second-order vibrational perturbation theory (VPT2) using the double-hybrid functional revDSD-PBEP86-D3BJ/jun-cc-pVTZ.
Rationale & Citation: Puzzarini, Barone, and co-workers have demonstrated that revDSD-PBEP86 provides harmonic and anharmonic force fields of quality comparable to canonical MP2/cc-pVTZ but at significantly reduced computational cost, predicting ground-state rotational constants within 0.1–0.2% of experiment for rigid and semi-rigid molecules (Puzzarini & Barone, J. Chem. Theory Comput., 2020, 16, 3110-3119; Biczysko et al., Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys., 2010, 12, 8135-8149).

- [ ] **Cycle 7:** Suggestion 4: Native Python Hybridization Engine for revDSD Analytic Dispersion and Double-Hybrid Energy/Force Evaluation in Open-Source Backends.
Actionable Recommendation: Implement a dedicated mathematical hybridization module in TORQ's Python layer that calculates revDSD-PBEP86 energy and nuclear gradient contributions by extracting exact exchange and MP2 correlation contributions (c_HF = 0.69, c_MP2-OS = 0.52, c_MP2-SS = 0.43) from PySCF or Psi4 routines, coupled with D3BJ empirical dispersion corrections via dftd3-python/torch-dftd.
Rationale & Citation: Open-source engines (PySCF, Psi4) provide robust SCF, DFT, and MP2 modules but often lack native end-to-end analytic gradient support for specific double-hybrid functionals like revDSD-PBEP86-D3BJ. Orchestrating this mixing inside TORQ allows the Open-Source Pathway to reach double-hybrid precision without commercial software dependencies (Kozuch & Martin, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys., 2011, 13, 20104-20107; Santra et al., J. Chem. Theory Comput., 2019, 15, 236-247).

points.source_text:
- [ ] **Cycle 7:** Suggestion 5: Harmonic Kivelson-Wilson Semi-Analytic Quartic Centrifugal Distortion Evaluation in Tiers 4–7.
Actionable Recommendation: Equip intermediate calculation tiers (DFT/MP2) with a semi-analytic module that derives Watson's quartic centrifugal distortion constants (DJ, DJK, DK, d1, d2 in S-reduction; Delta_J, Delta_JK, Delta_K, delta_J, delta_K in A-reduction) directly from the harmonic Cartesian force constants (Hessian) and the geometrical derivatives of the moment of inertia tensor (dI_alphabeta / dQ_k), bypassing the need for cubic force fields.
Rationale & Citation: Kivelson and Wilson demonstrated that quartic centrifugal distortion parameters (H04 terms) depend solely on equilibrium geometry and the harmonic force field (Kivelson & Wilson, J. Chem. Phys., 1952, 20, 1575-1579; Watson, J. Chem. Phys., 1967, 46, 1935-1949). Implementing this formulation enables mid-tier DFT calculations (e.g., B3LYP-D3/def2-TZVP) to generate physically sound quartic distortion parameters for initial SPCAT predictions at low cost.

points.source_text:
- [ ] **Cycle 7:** Suggestion 6: Core-Valence (CV) and Scalar Relativistic Corrections for Pinnacle Tier 11 (CFOUR) Rotational Constants.
Actionable Recommendation: For Tier 11 pinnacle calculations using CFOUR, implement additive corrections to the equilibrium rotational constants: B_best = B_e(CCSD(T)/CBS) + Delta B_CV + Delta B_SR. Compute Delta B_CV via all-electron versus frozen-core CCSD(T)/cc-pCVTZ calculations and Delta B_SR using second-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess (DKH2) or X2C scalar relativistic Hamiltonians.
Rationale & Citation: Modern high-resolution microwave experiments achieve sub-kHz precision. Neglecting core-valence electron correlation introduces structural deviations that alter Be by 0.2–0.5%, significantly exceeding the residual CBS extrapolation error (Heckert, Gauss, & Stanton, J. Chem. Phys., 2005, 123, 064302; Puzzarini, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys., 2013, 15, 6596-6607). Adding CV and scalar relativistic corrections ensures true sub-chemical accuracy.

points.source_text:
- [ ] **Cycle 7:** Suggestion 7: Dynamic Asymmetry Parameter (Ray's kappa) Evaluation for Automated Watson Reduction (A vs. S) and Representation Selection.
Actionable Recommendation: Implement an automated decision step in TORQ's calculation engine that calculates Ray's asymmetry parameter kappa = (2B - A - C)/(A - C) and automatically assigns Watson's Hamiltonian representation (Ir for prolate tops, IIIl/IIIr for oblate tops) and reduction scheme. When |kappa| > 0.90 (near symmetric top), enforce Watson's S-reduction (DJ, DJK, DK, d1, d2) over the A-reduction to prevent numerical instabilities.
Rationale & Citation: Watson's A-reduction exhibits severe accidental indeterminacies and denominator singularities for molecules approaching the prolate or oblate symmetric top limit, whereas the S-reduction remains mathematically robust and continuous (Watson, Vib. Spectra Struct., 1977, 6, 1-89; Pickett, J. Mol. Spectrosc., 1991, 148, 371-377). Dynamically selecting the reduction preserves numerical integrity in downstream SPFIT fitting.

points.source_text: - [ ] **Cycle 9:** CENSO-Inspired Multi-Stage Screening Cascade Across the 11 Tiers: Structure the transition of raw conformer ensembles from CREST/GOAT into the 11-Tier engine via a 4-part hierarchical screening strategy: Part 1: GFN2-xTB / MLFF single points with aggressive energy cutoffs (ΔE > 5.0 kcal/mol); Part 2: Cheap composite DFT (e.g., r2SCAN-3c or B97-3c in the Open-Source/ORCA pathways) geometry relaxation and rotational constant clustering; Part 3: Intermediate revDSD-PBEP86 / DLPNO-CCSD(T) single points on remaining candidates; Part 4: High-tier CFOUR CCSD(T)/VPT2 on top candidate conformers. Rationale & Citation: Directly dispatching hundreds of raw conformers from enumerators to ab initio engines produces unacceptable computational cost; multi-stage energetic sorting reduces DFT/CC workloads by 70–90% while guaranteeing the global minimum is retained (Grimme et al., J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2021, 17, 7711–7724; Hansen et al., J. Chem. Phys. 2022, 156, 174108).

points.source_text: - [ ] **Cycle 10:** Automated Boys-Bernardi BSSEOptimization.cmp Compound Script Integration in the ORCA Pathway: In the ORCA execution driver (orchestrator/cochem_orca_runner.py), mandate that whenever Tier 3/4 calculations (T3O-30min, T3O-3h) are run on non-covalent complexes with basis sets smaller than quadruple-zeta (e.g., def2-TZVPP or jun-cc-pVTZ), the driver must disallow raw '! Opt' and automatically wrap the input in ORCA's official BSSEOptimization.cmp compound script, parsing both uncorrected (E_raw) and counterpoise-corrected (E_CP) stationary geometries and energies into the pipeline state. Rationale: Plain geometry optimization on non-covalent van der Waals complexes without counterpoise gradients severely overbinds complexes due to BSSE (+4.1 pm shift in R at cc-pVTZ, causing ~2.8% error in rotational constant B). Using BSSEOptimization.cmp ensures optimization directly on the CP-corrected PES using analytical gradients. (Citations: Method Matrix v4.2, Section 4.7 & 12.5; Kruse et al., J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2012, 8, 2844–2853).

points.source_text: - [ ] **Cycle 10:** Geometrical Counterpoise (gCP) Dispersion-Harmonization Guardrail for Semi-Empirical and 3c Tiers: In TORQ's lower-tier engine, implement a parameter validation guardrail that checks the exact composition of composite DFT methods. If the selected method is r2SCAN-3c, TORQ must strictly block the injection of external D4 or gCP flags because both are internally parameterized. Conversely, if wB97X-3c is selected, TORQ must enforce D4 inclusion while prohibiting gCP (as BSSE is deliberately absorbed by D4 damping in wB97X-3c). For uncorrected DFT/semi-empirical tiers (e.g., HF/MINIX or B3LYP/def2-SVP), TORQ must automatically trigger the standalone gcp library to add geometry-dependent atom-pairwise BSSE corrections. Rationale: Double-counting BSSE corrections or dispersion damping (e.g., stacking gCP on methods already corrected or adding D4 to VV10 non-local functionals like ωB97M-V) catastrophically ruins the potential energy surface and equilibrium distances. (Citations: Grimme et al., J. Chem. Phys. 2015, 143, 054107; Method Matrix v4.2, Section 9A).

points.title: Automated Wavefunction Stability Guardrail Across Open-Source (PySCF) and ORCA Pathways
points.reason: SCF stability checks are useful; state-constrained jobs need target preservation rather than forced lowest root.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Cycle 10:** Automated Wavefunction Stability Guardrail Across Open-Source (PySCF) and ORCA Pathways: In the Open-Source and ORCA drivers, inject an automated post-SCF stability analysis (%scf stab end in ORCA, and mf.stability() in PySCF) for all open-shell and transition-state calculations. If an internal (RHF -> UHF or UKS -> UKS) or external instability is detected, TORQ must reject the converged solution, apply an orbital rotation along the negative eigenvalue eigenvector of the electronic Hessian, and re-solve SCF to obtain the true electronic ground state. Rationale: Standard SCF algorithms routinely converge to stationary saddle points or higher-energy local minima on the electronic orbital rotation surface, yielding false vibrational frequencies and corrupted spin densities. (Citations: Seeger & Pople, J. Chem. Phys. 1977, 66, 3045–3050; Bauernschmitt & Ahlrichs, J. Chem. Phys. 1996, 104, 9047–9052).

points.source_text: - [ ] **Cycle 10:** Yamaguchi Approximate Spin Projection Engine for the Open-Source revDSD Pathway: In the Open-Source pathway (cochem_torq/open_source/revdsd.py), where broken-symmetry (BS) unrestricted calculations are performed for open-shell or biradicaloid systems, implement the native Yamaguchi approximate spin projection formula: E_pure = (E_BS * <S^2>_HS - E_HS * <S^2>_BS) / (<S^2>_HS - <S^2>_BS). TORQ must automatically orchestrate the corresponding high-spin (HS) triplet/multiplet single-point calculation, compute E_pure, and store both raw and spin-projected energies in the execution pipeline. Rationale: Open-source double-hybrid DFT parameterizations (such as revDSD-PBEP86) lack native analytic spin-projection kernels in standard PySCF/Psi4 drivers; broken-symmetry solutions for open-shell complexes suffer from severe spin contamination that distorts relative conformer energies by up to 5–15 kcal/mol. (Citations: Yamaguchi et al., Chem. Phys. Lett. 1988, 149, 437–442; Kitagawa et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 4039–4048).

points.title: CABS Singles BSSE-Quenching Verification in the Restrictive CFOUR Pathway
points.reason: CFOUR F12 support and ORCA %scf syntax are conflated; 5% CABS ratio and CBS vanishing test are not justified.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Cycle 10:** CABS Singles BSSE-Quenching Verification in the Restrictive CFOUR Pathway: In the CFOUR calculation launcher for Tier 11 analytic CCSD(T)-F12 calculations, configure an automated sanity check that validates the Complementary Auxiliary Basis Set (CABS) singles correction. TORQ must verify that the CABS correction properly vanishes at the complete basis set limit and that the ratio of CABS singles energy to the total correlation energy does not exceed 5%. If CABS singles divergence occurs due to near-linear dependencies in the auxiliary basis, the run must be intercepted and automatically re-conditioned with an eigenvalue threshold %scf SThresh 1e-6. Rationale: Explicitly correlated F12 methods dramatically eliminate BSSE, but ill-conditioned auxiliary basis sets (CABS) can introduce numerical singularities into analytic second derivatives, destroying vibrational frequencies. (Citations: Adler, Knizia & Werner, J. Chem. Phys. 2007, 127, 224106; Puzzarini & Stanton, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 2023, 25, 1423–1435).

points.title: GPU-Accelerated Double-Precision (10^-11 Ha) Integral Screening & Basis Linear-Dependence Guardrail
points.reason: Overlap conditioning needs recorded truncation and energy/gradient sensitivity; universal 1e-11 Ha is unjustified.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Cycle 10:** GPU-Accelerated Double-Precision (10^-11 Ha) Integral Screening & Basis Linear-Dependence Guardrail: In cochem_system_config.py, when brokering jobs to GPU via gpu4pyscf, implement an automated pre-flight matrix condition check on the atomic orbital overlap matrix S. If the minimum eigenvalue λ_min(S) < 10^-6 (common when adding diffuse calendar sets like jun-cc-pVTZ to hydrogen atoms in complexes), TORQ must automatically activate canonical orthonormalization with dynamic orbital projection rather than raw Cholesky decomposition, while verifying that the GPU kernel preserves FP64 precision with energy residuals < 10^-11 Ha. Rationale: Diffuse basis functions in non-covalent complexes frequently lead to linear dependence. On GPUs, numerical precision loss in single or mixed precision can cause SCF oscillations or catastrophic gradient errors. (Citations: Wu et al., arXiv:2404.09452, 2024; Method Matrix v4.2, Section 8.3 & 12.5).

points.title: Active Learning Adaptive Grid Refinement (AL-PES) for Floppy Dihedral Scans

points.source_text: - [ ] **Cycle 2:** 8. Active Learning Adaptive Grid Refinement (AL-PES) for Floppy Dihedral Scans: Replace the uniform grid scanning protocol in Section 3.3 with an Active Learning Potential Energy Surface (AL-PES) adaptive sampling algorithm. Instead of evaluating rigid 5° or 10° increments, TORQ must initialize a sparse 30° grid using AIMNet2, fit a 1D/2D periodic Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) or cubic spline surrogate, and actively query new sample points only where the energy curvature |\nabla^2 E| or the AIMNet2 ensemble standard deviation \sigma_E exceeds user-defined tolerance thresholds (> 0.2 kcal/mol). Rationale & Citation: Adaptive sparse grid sampling reduces the number of electronic structure evaluations on multi-dimensional PES by 60–80% compared to uniform grid scans while maintaining sub-kJ/mol fidelity on barrier crests and minima (Kusne et al., Nature Comm. 2020; Dral et al., J. Chem. Phys. 2023).

points.source_text: - [ ] **Cycle 2:** 9. Automated Coupled Internal Rotor Identification via Wiberg Bond Index & Normal Mode Projection: Enhance Section 3.2 (HITL Isomer Interchange Detection) to automatically detect coupled internal rotations and ring-puckering coordinates. TORQ should compute Wiberg Bond Indices (WBI) and Mayer bond orders from Tier 1 MLFF electron densities or GFN2-xTB density matrices, identify dihedral bonds with order < 1.15, project low-frequency harmonic normal modes (< 150 cm^-1) onto internal coordinates, and rank coupled dihedral pairs (\phi_1, \phi_2) for 2D PES exploration. Rationale & Citation: For flexible molecules with multiple internal rotors, dihedrals are strongly coupled. Uncoupled 1D scans miss the lowest-energy interconversion pathways. Automated kinematic coupling detection prevents user omission of critical 2D coordinates (Spangler et al., PCCP 2021).

Master Equation and Kinetic Tunneling Correction Engine for Conformer Interconversion: Expand Section 3.4 (Energy Diagrams) to include a kinetic rate calculation module implementing 1D Eckart and WKB tunneling corrections alongside Canonical Transition State Theory (CTST): k(T) = \kappa(T) (k_B T / h) (Q^\ddagger / Q_R) \exp(-\Delta E^\ddagger / k_B T). TORQ must output temperature-dependent interconversion lifetimes (\tau_1/2) across the supersonic expansion regime (1–10 K) and room temperature (298 K) to determine whether conformers are kinetically trapped in molecular beams. Rationale & Citation: In rotational jet spectroscopy, barriers below ~400 cm^-1 (1.1 kcal/mol) allow conformational relaxation during supersonic cooling, wiping out high-energy conformers from the observed spectrum (Godfrey et al., JACS; Caminati et al.). Providing \tau_1/2 directly informs experimental spectroscopists whether a conformer is observable.

points.title: Quantitative Convergence Criteria for Dynamic Tier Escalation Protocol
points.reason: Compare relative energies on compatible references; inter-method stability is not accuracy or statistical convergence.
points.source_text: - [ ] **Cycle 2:** 13. Quantitative Convergence Criteria for Dynamic Tier Escalation Protocol: In Section 3.3 (Step 5: Convergence Threshold), replace the ambiguous phrase 'no significant improvement' with strict mathematical convergence tolerances: tier escalation terminates when the root-mean-square Cartesian coordinate displacement satisfies RMSD(R_n, R_{n-1}) < 0.005 Å, the relative electronic energy change satisfies |\Delta E_n - \Delta E_{n-1}| < 0.05 kcal/mol, and the rotational constants satisfy max(|\Delta A/A|, |\Delta B/B|, |\Delta C/C|) < 0.1%. Rationale & Citation: Vague stopping criteria violate the CoChem Anti-Spoofing and Zero-Mock directives. Explicit tolerances anchored to microwave experimental precision (< 0.1% for rotational constants) prevent wasted compute on redundant coupled-cluster cycles.

points.source_text: - [ ] **Cycle 3:** Deploy Multidimensional Wavefront Propagation for Multi-Rotor Scans: Replace naive sequential 1D/2D relaxed scans in Section 3.3 with the Wavefront Propagation algorithm. When scanning coupled dihedrals (\phi_1, \phi_2), optimizations at grid point (i, j) are concurrently seeded from all adjacent converged neighboring points min{E(i\pm 1, j), E(i, j\pm 1)}, completely eliminating scan-direction hysteresis and false barrier artifacts caused by sterically trapped dihedrals. Rationale & Citation: Qiu, Smith, Stern, Feng, & Wang (2020) 'Driving torsion scans with wavefront propagation', J. Chem. Phys. 152:244116.

Actionable Recommendation: For molecules containing internal rotors (-CH3, -OH, -NH2) identified in Section 3.2, augment the dynamic cascading PES protocol to fit 1D/2D periodic torsional energy slices to a truncated Fourier expansion V(alpha) = 0.5 * V3 * (1 - cos 3alpha) + 0.5 * V6 * (1 - cos 6alpha). Rationale & Citation: Internal rotation produces A-E tunneling state splittings in microwave spectra that cannot be reproduced by standard rigid-rotor or isolated-conformer Hamiltonians (Spahn et al., J. Mol. Spectrosc., 2008, 248, 149-160; Kisiel et al., J. Chem. Phys., 2013, 138, 194303). Extracting V3/V6 directly from the cascading PES allows downstream modeling with codes like ERHAM or XIAM.

Rev., 2016, 116, 5003-5034; Barone et al., Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys., 2014, 16, 1759-1787). Continuous inertia tracking provides accurate vibrationally averaged effective constants.

Theory Comput. 2021; Bunker & Jensen, Molecular Symmetry and Spectroscopy).

Rationale & Citations: Mitigates automated transition state search failures through expert human spatial intervention (Hermes et al., J. Chem. Phys. 2023; Asundham et al., ChemRxiv 2024).

points.source_text: - [ ] **Cycle 8:** Multi-Tier Convergence Delta Visualizer for the Dynamic 'Expand Out' Protocol: Build a CascadingConvergenceMonitorWidget that plots real-time RMSD geometry change (Delta RMSD in A) and relative energy change (Delta Delta E in kJ/mol or cm^-1) across consecutive tiers (e.g., Tier 3 -> Tier 4 -> Tier 5) for each stationary point. The UI highlights converged points in green when Delta E < 0.1 kJ/mol and Delta RMSD < 0.005 A, alerting the user to halt expensive expansions on flat regions. Rationale & Citations: Formalizes convergence criteria in composite quantum chemistry workflows to stop unneeded compute cycles (Karton, Int. J. Quantum Chem. 2021; Feller-Peterson-Dixon composite schemes).

points.title: Automated Redundant Internal Coordinate (DLC) Transfer and Constraint Preservation
